title: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
keyIdea: Reverse the flow: DFS from the Pacific edges (top, left) and from the Atlantic edges (bottom, right), only stepping to neighbours that are as high or higher. Cells reached by both floods are the answer.

approaches.name: Search downhill from every cell
approaches.idea: For each cell, follow water to equal or lower neighbours and see which edges it reaches.
approaches.why: A fresh search of up to m·n cells starts from each of the m·n cells.

approaches.name: DFS uphill from both oceans
approaches.idea: dfs(edge cell, ocean): mark it, move to neighbours with height ≥ current. Two visited grids; answer = cells in both.
approaches.why: Each flood visits every cell at most once.

quiz.q: Why start from the ocean edges instead of from each cell?
options: Two floods (one per ocean) visit each cell once, instead of a full search per cell
It is the only correct way

quiz.q: When climbing up from an ocean, which neighbours can you move to?
options: Neighbours with height ≥ the current cell

quiz.q: Which edges belong to the Pacific?
What does a cell need to be in the answer?
options: It is reached by both the Pacific flood and the Atlantic flood
It is reached by either flood
